item.title: The Ursoaia Kiln (north-eastern Romania): a benchmark for Chalcolithic specialised pottery production
item.headline: A prehistoric kiln hints at pottery production beyond the household
item.summary: A large, repeatedly repaired kiln in Romania suggests intensive pottery production about 6,000 years ago. Its size alone cannot establish a community workshop.

evidence.question: What can kiln construction reveal about prehistoric craft production?
evidence.method: Magnetic survey, excavation, four radiocarbon dates on associated animal remains, and electron microscopy with elemental analysis.
evidence.limitations: Reconstructed capacity and temperatures are estimates; workshop organisation remains unresolved.

explainer.finding: A working surface exceeding seven square metres and repair traces indicate substantial, repeated use.
explainer.method: Researchers combined the excavated structure with dating and microscopic examination of heat-altered materials.
explainer.meaning: Removable slabs separated pots from the fire below: damaged components could be replaced between firings.
explainer.limits: Heat exposure is inferred, not directly measured. Who operated the kiln and distributed its pottery remains uncertain.
